# Conversation-first workspace

The workspace sidebar contains new conversation, searchable conversation history,
Settings and the signed-in account. Projects remain an internal ownership boundary;
the interface does not ask users to create or select one. Existing conversation
history and custom agents keep their original owner and internal scope.
=== docs/delivery.md
# Delivery: from the agent's changes to a merged pull request

A **delivery** is the GitHub side of one conversation's repository work: the branch AgentForge publishes to, the
commits it has pushed, and the pull request (with its checks and reviews). It is owned by the backend and driven by
the person from the Changes panel; the agent's `create_pull_request` tool uses the same service.

=== docs/github-app.md
# GitHub App setup

AgentForge signs people in with a **GitHub App** (not an OAuth App) and reads and
writes repositories with each person's own expiring user token, limited to what
both they and the App installation may do. No installation private key is used.

# The agent

One loop serves every message: the model gets the conversation, a system prompt and its tools; it calls tools until it
has what it needs, then answers in plain text. That text is the answer, exactly as written
(`apps/api/src/agentforge/subagents/runtime.py`).

## What was removed, and why

Earlier versions ran a router, a planner, stage agents and an independent verifier, and forced every run to end by
submitting a typed result with evidence. A reply that did not satisfy those rules was rewritten as `PARTIAL`, so a
plain "What would you like help with?" showed a "Partial result" banner. All of that is gone: no router, planner,
verifier, `submit_result`, `PARTIAL` status or run-details page. A run ends as:

| Outcome | When | Shown |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `COMPLETED` | the model answered | its text, as written |
| `FAILED` | the provider or a tool broke | the reason: a provider's own message, credentials removed |
| `CANCELLED` | the person pressed Stop | "Stopped." |

Older messages may still carry `PARTIAL`; they render as plain text.

## Limits

Nothing caps steps, tool calls, cost or time. Usage is still recorded for accounting, and Stop always works. The
numbers in the budget rows (`Budget`, `UNLIMITED_*`) exist because the ledger needs positive values; they are set
high enough never to refuse anything.

## Tools

| Group | Tools |
| --- | --- |
| Web | `web_search`, `fetch_webpage` |
| Repository (read only, pinned commit) | `list_repo_files`, `search_repo`, `read_repo_file`, `get_issue`, `get_pr_status` |
| Sandbox (needs `E2B_API_KEY`) | `bash`, `read`, `write`, `edit`, `grep`, `find`, `ls` |
| Pull request (needs GitHub App + `ENABLE_GITHUB_WRITES`) | `create_pull_request` |
| Files and history | `create_task_artifact`, `read_task_artifact`, `search_conversation_history`, `read_context_resource` |
| Skills (when the person has any switched on) | `use_skill`: loads a playbook by name; see [skills](skills.md) |
| Plugins (per conversation) | `slug__tool`, from the MCP servers the person connected; see [plugins](plugins.md) |

The sandbox (`integrations/e2b_sandbox.py`, `tools/sandbox_shell.py`) is created on first use and kept for the
conversation: files and installed packages stay between messages. It has internet access and holds no secrets. When a
repository is selected the backend uploads its pinned commit and commits it as `agentforge-base`; pull requests are opened
by the backend from `git diff agentforge-base`, so GitHub credentials never enter the sandbox.

## Approvals

A global setting (`GET/PUT /api/v1/settings/approval-mode`, default `ask`) applies to every conversation.

* **Ask me**: before `bash`, `write`, `edit` or `create_pull_request` the run stops and the chat shows an Approve /
  Decline card (`approval.required`) with exactly what will run: the whole command, the file content or the edit, or
  the pull request with every file it changes. It waits as long as it takes. Declining returns a normal tool result
  telling the agent the person said no. A command too long to show in full is refused before anyone is asked.
* **Approve for me**: nothing asks.

A plugin tool also asks in **Ask me** mode unless its server declares it read-only.

The mode is read before each call, so switching it releases a waiting card. Answers: `POST /api/v1/tool-approvals/{id}`.
Implementation: `tools/approvals.py`, hooked into `tools/gateway.py`.

  pids+=("$!")
  set +m
}

stop() {

  for pid in "${pids[@]}"; do kill -TERM -- "-$pid" 2>/dev/null || kill -TERM "$pid" 2>/dev/null; done
  wait 2>/dev/null

# Single-EC2 release configuration

This configuration hosts nginx, Next.js, FastAPI, one worker and PostgreSQL on
one Linux EC2 instance. Managed E2B remains the coding execution boundary; the
host never runs submitted repositories. No AWS account, instance, domain or
deployment was created. Docker Compose rendering is locally checkable without a
daemon; image builds, TLS and restart behavior need deployment-host qualification.
The web image runs Next.js's standalone server (`node server.js`, from
`output: "standalone"` in `apps/web/next.config.ts`) with only its traced
dependencies, not the full `node_modules`.

## Host and storage prerequisites

Use a patched Linux host with Docker Engine and Compose v2. Start with enough RAM
for a Next.js build and PostgreSQL; measure before choosing instance size. Bind
only TCP 80/443 publicly. Restrict SSH to an operator address or use Session
Manager. Do not publish 3000/8000/5432 or mount the Docker socket in application
containers. Security groups are the host's network boundary; see
[AWS security groups](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/ec2-security-groups.html).

Mount a persistent encrypted EBS volume at `/srv`, including
`/srv/agentforge/postgres`, `/srv/agentforge/artifacts` and a private backup
directory. Configure encryption before storing data, retain the data volume on
instance termination, monitor free space, and keep encrypted off-instance backups.
[EBS encryption](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/ebs-encryption.html)
protects the storage layer; application credentials still need separate access
control. The current artifact implementation requires POSIX filesystem behavior.
API and worker share the same artifact mount and UID/GID 10001; create the artifact
directory with owner `10001:10001`, mode `0700`. Backups contain user material.

Provision a DNS name and trusted certificate using your chosen certificate
manager. Install `fullchain.pem` and `privkey.pem` beneath `/etc/agentforge/tls`.
nginx redirects HTTP to HTTPS and uses TLS1.2/1.3. Certificate renewal is an
operator responsibility: replace files atomically, run `nginx -t` and reload the
proxy before expiry. The supplied proxy does not provide an HTTP ACME challenge
handler; use DNS validation or adapt the proxy for the selected certificate tool.

## Separate operator and runtime configuration

Copy `deploy.env.example` to `/etc/agentforge/deploy.env` and
`runtime.env.example` to `/etc/agentforge/runtime.env`, both mode `0600`. Replace
every placeholder. The files deliberately fail to launch as shipped. Never bake
provider keys, OAuth secrets, TLS keys or environment files into images.
`SITE_URL` (the public origin) is required: Compose refuses to render without it,
since the web image prerenders public pages with it.

`deploy.env` contains Compose interpolation, database bootstrap/admin URLs and a
distinct runtime password. It is **not** passed into API/worker containers.
`runtime.env` contains only runtime credentials and app settings. The database
initialization script creates `agentforge_admin` as the PostgreSQL administrator
and `agentforge` as a non-superuser with DML permissions and no schema creation.
Only the explicit `migration` service receives administrator URLs; tables created
by that administrator grant runtime access via default privileges. A pre-existing
database does not rerun init scripts: review and apply equivalent role/grant setup
before using this configuration with existing data.

The Docker subnet is `172.29.237.0/24`; nginx has `172.29.237.10`. FastAPI trusts
forwarded headers only from that address. If this conflicts with host networking,
change both the subnet/static address and `--forwarded-allow-ips` together. All
other app ports remain private. Access logs and OAuth-route error logs are disabled
# Application migrations

Run from `apps/api`:

```powershell
uv run alembic upgrade head
uv run alembic current
uv run alembic check
```

The connection URL comes from `agentforge.settings` and the ignored root or API `.env`. Credentials do not belong in `alembic.ini`.

The initial revision creates only `users`, `projects`, `agent_definitions`, `agent_definition_versions` and `tasks`. Alembic also maintains its own `alembic_version` table. PostgreSQL 16+ provides the `gen_random_uuid()` function used by primary key defaults.

For future changes, update the models, generate a new revision with `uv run alembic revision --autogenerate -m "Describe the change"`, and review the generated migration before applying it. Applied revisions must remain unchanged. Add later-phase tables in separate revisions.

Revision `0002_phase2` adds only the Phase 2 child harness tables: `agent_runs`, `tool_calls`, `budget_reservations`, `budget_operations` and `budget_transactions`. It preserves the Phase 1 schema. Reservations/operations support atomic accounting and crash-conservative usage; they are prerequisites for safe Phase 2 invocation, not Phase 3 orchestration tables. `task_steps`, artifacts, task events and LangGraph checkpoint tables remain deferred.

The Phase 2 revision was authored and source-reviewed without being applied. No upgrade/downgrade, database history or metadata-equivalence checks were run during that implementation. Perform them against an isolated database as part of the [Phase 2 handoff](../../../docs/phase-2.md).

# Plugins

A plugin is a remote [MCP](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) server the person connects, so the agent can use its tools
(look up library docs, read a Linear issue, search GitHub). Plugins are the one place the agent's tool set is open-ended,
so everything below exists to keep that safe.

## Using them

1. **The Plugins page** (sidebar → Plugins; there is no copy in Settings, and the old `/settings?section=plugins` link redirects here) is a quiet list: **Connected** plugins, then
   **Available** ones (about fifty, grouped by category, plus "Your own server"), each with its logo. Search and the category
   pills filter the list; **Add** (top right) or a row's **+** connects one. A plugin that signs in with OAuth sends the person to
   the service to sign in; one that takes a token asks for it in a dialog. Nothing is saved unless the server answers and lists
   at least one tool.
2. **The switch** on a connected plugin chooses whether new conversations start with it. A conversation keeps the plugins it
   started with. The message box has no plugin picker.
3. **Opening a connected plugin** shows its tools, a Refresh, its token and Remove. Each tool can be switched off there. Use it to drop tools the agent does not
   need (every tool adds to each request) or to keep a plugin read-only.
4. In **Ask me** mode a plugin tool waits for approval unless the server marks it read-only (`readOnlyHint`); the card shows
   the plugin, the tool and every argument. **Approve for me** never asks.

## How it works

| Piece | Where |
| --- | --- |
| Catalog (closed list we reviewed) | `plugins/catalog.py` |
| MCP client: Streamable HTTP, JSON or SSE answers, sessions, 404 → new session | `plugins/mcp.py` |
| OAuth: discovery, registration, PKCE, tokens | `plugins/oauth.py` |
| OAuth sign-in flow, callback binding, token renewal, revocation | `plugins/oauth_service.py`, `api/routes_plugins.py` (`/oauth/*`) |
| Tool names, schemas, read-only hints | `plugins/schema.py` |
| Connect, refresh, update, remove; per-conversation choice | `plugins/service.py`, `api/routes_plugins.py` |
| Giving a run its tools | `plugins/runtime.py`, `bootstrap.compose_runtime` |
| Gateway, approvals, audit | `tools/catalog.py` (`PluginTool`), `tools/gateway.py` |
| Storage | `plugin_connections`, `conversations.plugins_json` (migration `0015_plugins`) |

A connection stores the server address, an encrypted credential, and the tools the server listed when it was last read. When
a conversation's turn starts, the worker registers the tools of the plugins that conversation uses under the names
`slug__tool` (for example `linear__create_issue`), opens one MCP client per plugin for the run, and closes it with the run.
The tools are offered to whichever agent runs, beside its own. A failure to set plugins up never stops a turn; it runs
without them.

`GET/POST /api/v1/plugins`, `PATCH/DELETE /api/v1/plugins/{id}`, `POST /api/v1/plugins/{id}/refresh`; sessions take and return
`plugins` (a list of connection ids) on create, patch and read.

## Trust and safety

A plugin server is third-party code reached from our servers with the person's credential.

* **Network.** https only, port any, every address the name resolves to must be public, the connection goes to the checked
  address with TLS bound to the host name (resolved again on every request), redirects are never followed, responses are size
  limited. `PLUGIN_ALLOW_PRIVATE_NETWORK` relaxes this for local development and is refused in production.
# Skills

A skill is a written playbook for a kind of work: a name, a one-paragraph description, and instructions. The agent does not carry
every playbook in its prompt. It is told each skill's name and description, and loads the instructions only when a request fits.
Some skills ship with the app; people also write their own.

## Using them

* **The Skills tab of the Plugins page** (sidebar → Plugins → Skills; the old `/settings?section=skills` link redirects here) lists the built-in skills and the
  person's own as cards. Each has a switch. The person's own skills can be created, edited, imported from a `SKILL.md`, exported,
  and deleted. A built-in skill cannot be edited, but **Copy to my skills** makes an editable copy under a new name.
* **Typing `/name` at the start of a message** asks for that skill. Otherwise the agent decides: when a request clearly fits a skill's
  description it loads the skill first (the timeline shows "Loaded a skill").

## Built-in skills

| Name | For |
| --- | --- |
| `deep-research` | Sourced, cross-checked web research |
| `code-review` | Reviewing a diff, branch or area of code; prioritized findings |
| `debug-and-fix` | Reproducing, diagnosing and fixing a bug or failing test |
| `implement-feature` | Planning, building and verifying a feature |
| `write-tests` | Adding unit, integration or regression tests |
| `explore-codebase` | Explaining how an unfamiliar repository works |
| `pull-request` | Verifying work and opening a draft pull request |
| `write-report` | Documents and reports saved as downloadable files |
| `analyze-data` | Analysing CSV/JSON data with code in the workspace |
| `write-skill` | Helping a person write a new skill |

They are packaged files, `apps/api/src/agentforge/skills/builtin/<name>.md`, in the same `SKILL.md` format a person can import.
Adding or changing one is a code change: edit the file, and for a new one add its name to `ORDER` in `skills/builtin.py`.
`tests/test_skills.py` checks that every built-in is valid, fits one tool result, and names only tools that exist.

## The format

```
---
name: code-review
description: Review code changes and report prioritized findings. Use when asked to review a diff or pull request.
---
# Delivery: from the agent's changes to a merged pull request

A **delivery** is the GitHub side of one conversation's repository work: the branch AgentForge publishes to, the
commits it has pushed, and the pull request (with its checks and reviews). It is owned by the backend and driven by
the person from the Changes panel; the agent's `create_pull_request` tool uses the same service.

The sandbox holds no credentials. Every GitHub write is made by the API with the signed-in person's expiring user
token, re-checked live (`AuthorizedGitHubClient.authorize(write=True)`), fast-forward only, never forced.
Merge, close and mark-ready are **human-only**: they exist only as the endpoints below, never as agent tools.

## Lifecycle

```
none ──push──▶ branch ──open PR──▶ draft / open ──merge──▶ merged
                  ▲                    │   └────close────▶ closed
                  └──── push more ◀────┘
```

* Changes are the sandbox working tree compared with the last published state (`agentforge-pushed` tag; before the
  first push, `agentforge-base`, the pinned commit the repository was loaded at).
* A push commits those changes on top of the delivery's `head_sha` (first push: creates the branch at `base_sha`).
* Pushing and discarding are refused while a turn is running (`agent_running`), so the diff cannot race the agent.
* After merge or close, **reset** starts a fresh delivery from the updated base branch (the sandbox is reloaded).

## HTTP API

All routes are owner-scoped under `/api/v1/sessions/{session_id}/delivery`, return `Cache-Control: no-store`, and
use `HTTPException` with `detail` = a machine code (table below). Mutations take an `idempotency_key` (UUID):
repeating a key returns the stored outcome instead of acting twice.

# Delegated assignments

The default assistant (immutable `builtin/agent` version 3) can call
`delegate_task` with a short `title`, a self-contained `prompt`, and an optional
`mode` (`research` by default, or `work`). Existing tasks pinned to versions 1
and 2 retain their original definitions.

Delegation is synchronous, and independent assignments run in parallel. When the
main agent calls `delegate_task` several times in one reply, the children start
together and the agent receives every report once all have finished, in the order
it asked for them; it then verifies and integrates them. A reply that also calls
`bash`, `write` or `edit` stays strictly in order, as before. The tool description
is what teaches the model to launch independent assignments together (the agent
prompt is an immutable version). Work assignments share one workspace, so the
model is told to give parallel ones different files; `write` replaces a whole file,
so two children writing the same path would overwrite each other. A child that
fails or times out hands back its last few progress notes (`progress_notes`) so the
parent can build on its work. The child uses the configured model in a
separate conversation containing its assignment, platform instructions, and
authorized environment information. Parent messages are not automatically
copied. The conversation workspace and task-owned resources remain shared.

Research assignments cannot write files or execute commands. Work assignments
can use those tools only within the parent's grants, with the same approval
```

# AgentForge **Build with a coding agent. Keep the final say.** A conversational workspace where one agent researches the web, writes and runs code in an isolated sandbox, and prepares pull requests, while you approve every change before it happens. ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-3.12%20%7C%203.13-3776AB?logo=python&logoColor=white) ![FastAPI](https://img.shields.io/badge/FastAPI-009688?logo=fastapi&logoColor=white) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-16-000000?logo=nextdotjs&logoColor=white) ![PostgreSQL](https://img.shields.io/badge/PostgreSQL-4169E1?logo=postgresql&logoColor=white) ![E2B](https://img.shields.io/badge/Sandbox-E2B-ff8800) [Quick start](#quick-start) · [Features](#features) · [Architecture](#architecture) · [Configuration](#configuration) · [Deployment](#deployment) · [Documentation](#documentation)

## Why AgentForge Most coding agents either ask for permission constantly or none at all. AgentForge is built around a single honest agent loop and a clear approval model: - **One agent, no ceremony.** The model gets the conversation, a system prompt and its tools. It calls tools until it has what it needs, then answers in plain text, shown exactly as written. No router, planner or verifier rewrites it. - **You decide what runs.** In **Ask me** mode the agent stops before anything that changes something (a command, a file write or edit, a pull request) and shows an Approve / Decline card with exactly what will happen. In **Approve for me** mode it never asks. Stop ends a run at any time. - **Isolated by design.** Code runs in a persistent [E2B](https://e2b.dev) sandbox per conversation. The sandbox holds no secrets; GitHub writes are made by the backend with your own token, never from inside the sandbox. - **Observable.** Every run keeps its event history and a usage ledger, and can be traced to [Neatlogs](https://neatlogs.com) (metadata only by default). ## Features | | | | --- | --- | | **Research** | Web search (Exa, with Tavily as fallback) and page fetching with public-address and redirect checks. | | **Code in a sandbox** | `bash`, `read`, `write`, `edit`, `grep`, `find` and `ls` in a per-conversation E2B sandbox; files and installed packages persist between messages. | | **Repositories** | Select a GitHub repository per conversation. The agent reads a pinned commit, works on a copy and never sees your credentials. | | **Delivery to GitHub** | Review the diff in the Changes panel, publish a branch, open a draft pull request and watch its checks. Merge and close are human-only. | | **Live activity** | Notes, steps and the reply stream as the agent works, with a live context-size indicator and earlier steps folded away. | | **Plugins** | Connect remote [MCP](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) servers (a reviewed catalog of services, or your own) and choose them per conversation. | | **Skills** | Built-in and personal playbooks (code review, debugging, deep research, pull requests and more), loaded when a request fits or invoked with `/name`. | | **Delegation** | The agent can hand independent assignments to child runs that work in parallel under the parent's limits and approvals. | | **Custom agents** | Immutable, versioned agent definitions managed from Settings. | | **Durable conversations** | Saved history, queued follow-ups, source-linked summaries and retrieval of original inputs. | | **Sign-in** | GitHub App sign-in with revocable sessions, or a local bootstrap token for development. | ## Architecture ```mermaid flowchart LR Browser --> Proxy[Same-origin TLS proxy] Proxy --> Web[Next.js workspace] Proxy --> API[FastAPI identity and task API] API --> DB[(PostgreSQL: tasks, events, leases)] Worker[Python worker] --> DB Worker --> Agent[Agent loop: model, tools, plain-text answer] Agent --> Providers[Model and research providers] Agent --> E2B[Persistent E2B sandbox per conversation] Agent --> Approvals[Inline approval cards in the chat] Worker --> Artifacts[Private artifact storage] API --> Artifacts Worker --> GitHub[Draft pull requests, opened by the backend] ``` The API and the worker are separate processes that coordinate through PostgreSQL: the API accepts requests and serves events, the worker leases tasks and runs the agent loop. Any OpenAI-compatible model endpoint can be used. ```text apps/ api/ FastAPI service, worker, agent runtime, migrations and tests (Python) web/ Next.js App Router workspace and landing pages (TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, shadcn/ui) docs/ Reference documentation infra/ Single-host deployment (Docker Compose, nginx) and the E2B sandbox template scripts/ Local setup, dev runner and release checks assets/ Brand master artwork ``` ## Quick start **Requirements:** Python 3.12 or 3.13, [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/), Node.js 24, pnpm 10.34.6 (via corepack) and a local PostgreSQL 16+ server. Dependencies are locked in `apps/api/uv.lock` and `apps/web/pnpm-lock.yaml`. ```sh # 1. Check tools, create .env from the template if absent, install dependencies scripts/dev-setup.sh # 2. Edit .env: set DATABASE_URL and the LLM_* block (see Configuration below) # 3. Create the schema, then a local sign-in identity (cd apps/api && uv run alembic upgrade head) (cd apps/api && uv run python -m agentforge.auth.bootstrap --write-env) # 4. Verify the setup: one PASS/FAIL line per requirement (cd apps/api && uv run python -m agentforge.doctor) # 5. Start the API (:8000), the worker and the web app (:3000) together; Ctrl-C stops all scripts/dev.sh ``` Open , choose **Get started** and enter the `LOCAL_BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN` from your `.env`. > `scripts/dev-setup.sh --migrate` applies the migrations for you. It never overwrites an existing `.env`. ## Configuration Settings live in an ignored root `.env`. [`.env.example`](.env.example) is the template and is kept to what you must or may set; every other setting has a safe default. The API refuses to start on invalid settings and names the fields, never their values. | Setting | Purpose | | --- | --- | | `DATABASE_URL` | PostgreSQL connection (required). | | `AUTH_MODE`, `LOCAL_USER_ID`, `LOCAL_BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN` | Local sign-in; filled in by the bootstrap command. | | `LLM_MODEL`, `LLM_API_KEY`, `LLM_CONTEXT_WINDOW_TOKENS`, `LLM_*_USD_PER_MILLION` | Your OpenAI-compatible model (required to chat). | | `E2B_API_KEY` | Enables the coding sandbox. | | `EXA_API_KEY` / `TAVILY_API_KEY` | Enables web search; either works alone. | | `NEATLOGS_API_KEY` | Enables tracing. | | `PLUGIN_ENCRYPTION_KEY` | Lets people save plugin tokens and sign in to plugins (32+ random characters). | | `ENABLE_GITHUB_WRITES` | Lets the agent open draft pull requests (needs a GitHub App). | | `SITE_URL` | The public origin, set at web build time for the social card, sitemap and robots. | For GitHub sign-in and private repositories, create a GitHub App as described in [docs/github-app.md](docs/github-app.md). The complete list of settings with their defaults is in [docs/configuration.md](docs/configuration.md). `API_ORIGIN` (in `apps/web/.env.local`, default `http://localhost:8000`) is the server-side origin that Next.js rewrites `/api/` to; deployments route `/api/` straight to FastAPI on the same origin. ## Development ```sh # API tests (unittest) cd apps/api && uv run python -m unittest discover -s tests # Web: tests, lint and types cd apps/web pnpm test:web pnpm lint pnpm exec next typegen && pnpm exec tsc --noEmit ``` Run the whole release gate from the repository root: ```sh uv run --project apps/api python scripts/release_checks.py ``` It runs the unit checks, database fixtures on uniquely named disposable PostgreSQL databases and the frontend lint, types and build, then writes private logs and a machine-readable receipt under the ignored `.local/releases/`. The fixtures migrate and remove only the databases they create, and never call paid providers. The PostgreSQL user needs `CREATE DATABASE`, or set `TEST_DATABASE_ADMIN_URL`. Use pnpm 10.34.6: a global pnpm 12 is incompatible with this lockfile. The same checks run in [GitHub Actions](.github/workflows/ci.yml). Adding a migration is covered in [apps/api/alembic/README.md](apps/api/alembic/README.md). ## Deployment [`infra/deploy`](infra/deploy/README.md) contains a single-host configuration: nginx with TLS, the Next.js standalone server, FastAPI, one worker and PostgreSQL on one Linux instance, with non-root services, least-privilege runtime database access, encrypted persistent storage, backups and restore procedures. Production requires `AUTH_MODE=github_app` and https origins. This is a single-instance configuration: there is downtime during coordinated backups and no high-availability claim. The container images and a hosted deployment have not been qualified on a real host yet, so treat the first deployment as something to verify. ## Documentation | Topic | Page | | --- | --- | | How the agent works: loop, tools, approvals, limits | [docs/agent.md](docs/agent.md) | | Tool calling, validation and failure handling | [docs/agent-harness.md](docs/agent-harness.md) | | System prompt and tool descriptions | [docs/agent-prompts.md](docs/agent-prompts.md) | | Live notes, steps and streamed replies | [docs/live-activity.md](docs/live-activity.md) | | Conversation context, history and compaction | [docs/context-management.md](docs/context-management.md) | | Durable delivery, queued follow-ups and summaries | [docs/conversation-reliability.md](docs/conversation-reliability.md) | | Workspace behavior and URLs | [docs/conversation-ux.md](docs/conversation-ux.md) | | Branches, pull requests, checks and merging | [docs/delivery.md](docs/delivery.md) | | Plugins (MCP servers) | [docs/plugins.md](docs/plugins.md) | | Skills | [docs/skills.md](docs/skills.md) | | Delegated assignments | [docs/subagents.md](docs/subagents.md) | | GitHub App setup | [docs/github-app.md](docs/github-app.md) | | Every setting and its default | [docs/configuration.md](docs/configuration.md) | | Neatlogs tracing | [docs/neatlogs.md](docs/neatlogs.md) | | Sandbox usage and cost reporting | [docs/sandbox-usage.md](docs/sandbox-usage.md) | | E2B sandbox template | [infra/e2b/README.md](infra/e2b/README.md) | | Single-host deployment | [infra/deploy/README.md](infra/deploy/README.md) | ## Security - The sandbox has internet access and holds no secrets; credentials never enter it. - GitHub writes use the signed-in person's own expiring token, are re-checked on every call, are fast-forward only and are never forced. - Plugin servers are reached over https only, to public addresses only, without following redirects. - Plugin credentials are stored encrypted, and provider errors shown in the chat have credentials removed. Please report a suspected vulnerability privately to the maintainers rather than opening a public issue.
